series.label: Thermoplastic resin prices
series.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED
series.note: Producer Price Index for thermoplastic resins and plastics materials. PVC sits in this basket alongside polyethylene, polypropylene and polystyrene. It is the closest free, official stand-in for the PVC contract price Plastics News used to publish.

series.label: Plastics pipe and fitting prices
series.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED
series.note: Producer Price Index for U.S. plastics pipe and pipe fitting manufacturers. This is the selling-price side of the business, so the gap between it and the resin index is a rough read on converter margins.

series.label: Crude oil, WTI spot
series.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, via FRED
series.note: West Texas Intermediate crude at Cushing, Oklahoma. Oil drives PVC costs in Europe and Asia, where ethylene is made from naphtha. In the U.S. its effect on PVC is indirect: it moves sentiment, freight and export pricing more than it moves the resin's own feedstock cost.

series.label: Natural gas, Henry Hub spot
series.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, via FRED
series.note: U.S. PVC is made from ethylene cracked from ethane, a natural gas liquid, plus chlorine made with a lot of electricity. That makes natural gas the more direct cost indicator for domestic PVC than crude oil.
